rulings.restated: Input — Does any of these apply: a SARSEP; a SEP plan whose contribution rate is not a whole percentage or is more than 25%; a SIMPLE IRA plan of an employer that allows the higher contribution limits of section 117 of the SECURE 2.0 Act; contributions for yourself to more than one plan, or to a qualified plan (such as a solo 401(k)); salary reduction contributions or elective deferrals to any other plan in 2025 (such as a 401(k) or 403(b) through an employer); Roth SEP or Roth SIMPLE contributions; or contributions that are more than the maximum deductible amount?
rulings.model: Pub. 560 says 'the table and the worksheets in chapter 5 apply only to self-employed individuals who have only one defined contribution plan... A SEP plan is treated as a profit-sharing plan.' The worksheet requires step 9 'If you made any elective deferrals to your self-employed plan.' The screen excludes only SIMPLE IRA plans of section-117 employers, so an ordinary SIMPLE IRA with salary reduction contributions for yourself is not excluded.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; project retained. The chapter 5 Rate and Deduction Worksheets, with their step 9 for elective deferrals, are used only for the SEP (person.sep_s1 to sep_s21); a SIMPLE IRA is figured under chapter 3, where 'Contributions are made up of salary reduction contributions and employer contributions ... which you can deduct' (p560 p. 16, chapter 3, SIMPLE IRA Plan): person.simple_deduction is the salary reduction contributions (person.simple_deferral, with catch-up) plus the matching or nonelective contribution, refused above the limits (person.simple_excess). So an ordinary SIMPLE IRA with salary reduction contributions for yourself is supported, not misfigured; salary reduction contributions to any other plan, a SARSEP and more than one plan are screened.

rulings.restated: Input — Does any of these apply to this person: church employee income (wages from a church that elected exemption from social security and Medicare taxes); being a minister, a member of a religious order or a Christian Science practitioner, or having an approved Form 4361 or Form 4029; net earnings from self-employment from a partnership (Schedule K-1, box 14, code A) or other self-employment income not on a Schedule C (such as director's fees, fiduciary fees, or fees as a fee-basis state or local government employee); farm income (Schedule F) or Conservation Reserve Program payments; electing an optional method (Schedule SE Part II); a chapter 11 bankruptcy case; community income on a separate return; self-employment income exempt under an international social security agreement or earned as a U.S. citizen employed by a foreign government; or tips reported on Form 4137 or wages on Form 8919?
rulings.model: The screen leaves out cases the IRS text says change Schedule SE line 2. For statutory employees: 'If you were a statutory employee, don't include the net profit or (loss) from Schedule C, line 31, on Schedule SE, line 2.' For notaries: 'Notary public. Do not enter your net profit from line 31 on Schedule SE (Form 1040), line 2.' The screen also omits railroad tier 1 compensation, which belongs on line 8a, yet line 2 is still set to the full Schedule C total.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: defect, fixed (BUG-0076). Statutory employee income and notary fees are refused on each Schedule C (sc.statutory, 'income you received as a statutory employee ... or fees you received as a notary public'; checked: sc.statutory true refuses se_line2, se_line12 and Schedule 2 line 4), so that part of the model's reason is wrong. Railroad tier 1 compensation is not: Schedule SE line 8a is 'Total social security wages and tips (total of boxes 3 and 7 on Form(s) W-2) and railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation' (f1040sse p. 1, line 8a), the project binds line 8a to person.wages (boxes 3 and 7 only; se.yaml line 8a label drops the tier 1 words), and person.rrta refuses only Schedule 3 line 11 and Form 8959, not Schedule SE. Case: single filer, railroad W-2 with $170,000 tier 1 compensation (boxes 3 to 7 empty), Schedule C profit $30,000, person.rrta yes: the project gives Schedule SE line 12 $4,238.87, Schedule 1 line 15 $2,119.44 and Form 1040 line 11a $197,880.56, unrefused (line 24 refuses); with tier 1 on line 8a line 9 is $6,100 and line 12 $1,559.85, line 13 $779.93, AGI $199,220.07. Either add tier 1 compensation to line 8a or make person.rrta refuse person.se_line2 (or name railroad compensation in person.se_screen). Owner ruling: refuse. A person with a Schedule C who answers yes to the railroad question is refused at Schedule SE (person.se_rrta); line 8a's label is now the printed text.

rulings.model: The screen leaves out statutory employees and notaries public. The instructions say for statutory employees 'do not report this amount on Schedule SE (Form 1040), line 2', and for notaries 'Do not enter your net profit from line 31 on Schedule SE (Form 1040), line 2', yet se_line2 adds every Schedule C.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; project retained. Statutory employee income and notary fees are refused on each Schedule C (sc.statutory), so every Schedule C that reaches this line is one whose net profit Schedule SE line 2 takes; the second's filter excludes nothing the tool admits. Railroad retirement compensation with a Schedule C is refused (person.se_rrta), so line 8a is the W-2 boxes 3 and 7 for every person who reaches it.

rulings.model: The restatement sums Schedule C net profit across all of the person's businesses. Pub 560 limits the deduction to compensation 'from the business that has the plan' and to '20% of your net earnings... from the business that has the plan'. The two differ when the person has more than one Schedule C.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: defect, fixed (BUG-0078). Pub. 560 (2025) p. 7, Earned income: 'If you have more than one business, but only one has a retirement plan, only the earned income from that business is considered for that plan'; p. 11: 25% of the compensation 'from the business that has the plan'; p. 40 note: 'can't be more than 20% of your net earnings ... from the business that has the plan'. The project's Step 1 is person.sc_total, the person's Schedule C net profit from all businesses, and nothing asks which business has the plan or refuses a person with two or more Schedules C and a SEP or SIMPLE plan (person.plan_screen covers more than one plan, not more than one business). Evaluated: stage14.sep.basic (one business, $100,000 profit, SEP 25%) gives Step 21 $18,587.04; the same return with a second Schedule C of $30,000 gives sep_s1 $130,000.00 and Step 21 $24,163.16, and a $20,000 contribution is admitted in full (sep_excess false, s1.line16 $20,000.00), more than the plan's business alone allows. The SIMPLE compensation (person.simple_comp, Schedule SE line 4c of all businesses) has the same reach. The register entry amb.2025.f7206_plan_attribution (owner accepted) rests on 'The SEP and SIMPLE limits are figured on the person's net earnings from all businesses', which this passage contradicts; the remedy (ask which business has the plan, or refuse a plan with more than one business) is for the owner. Owner ruling: a SEP or SIMPLE plan with more than one Schedule C is refused (person.plan_screened).

rulings.model: Step 2 uses this person's Schedule SE line 13, which matches 'deduction for self-employment tax from Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15.' However, Schedule SE line 8a is bound to the line wages, which sums w2.wages. Line 8a must be the 'total of boxes 3 and 7 on Form(s) W-2,' and the text given does not show whether w2.wages is boxes 3 plus 7.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; restatement accepted. w2.wages is 'Add social security wages and social security tips', the sum of w2.box3 and w2.box7 (forms/2025/w2.yaml; amb.2025.ss_wages, owner approved), so Schedule SE line 8a is boxes 3 and 7 as the form says, and Step 2 is this person's own Schedule SE line 13 as the worksheet says (p560 p. 39). The tier 1 railroad compensation that line 8a also includes is not added; that defect is ruled under person.se_screen and changes this step for a railroad employee with a Schedule C.

rulings.restated: Add w2.one over every confirmed w2 entry, within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: The IRS condition is "had more than one employer for 2025", but the restatement counts confirmed W-2 entries. One employer can issue several Forms W-2, which would wrongly count as more than one employer.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The W-2 collection is keyed by employer, and repeated forms from one employer are consolidated into one entry ("Keyed by employer within person; consolidate repeated forms for the same employer explicitly", forms/2025/w2.yaml collection note), so the count of entries is the count of employers that "had more than one employer for 2025" (i1040gi p. 117) asks for. No change to the data.

rulings.model: The IRS test is 'had more than one employer,' but this line counts Form W-2 entries. The text given does not say whether a count of W-2s can stand in for a count of employers, for example when one employer issues more than one W-2.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: defect, fixed (BUG-0076). The count is right only if each w2 entry is one employer: the collection note says 'Keyed by employer within person; consolidate repeated forms for the same employer explicitly' (forms/2025/w2.yaml), but the filer is asked only 'List stable keys for Form W-2 - Social Security boxes by employer' (interview/questions-2025.yaml, $w2) and nothing tells them to combine two Forms W-2 from one employer. i1040gi p. 117: credit only if you 'had more than one employer', and 'if any one employer withheld more than $10,918.20, you can't claim the excess on your return'. Case: one employer issues two Forms W-2, each $100,000 box 3 and $6,200 box 4, entered as two entries: employers = 2, overcount = 0, Schedule 3 line 11 = $1,481.80, where the instructions allow no credit (that employer withheld $12,400). The $w2 question (and the collection prompt) should say one entry per employer, combining every Form W-2 from the same employer; no change to the arithmetic. The $w2 question now asks for one key per employer and to combine an employer's several Forms W-2 under it.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The W-2 collection is keyed by employer, and repeated forms from one employer are consolidated into one entry ('Keyed by employer within person; consolidate repeated forms for the same employer explicitly', forms/2025/w2.yaml), so the count of entries over the limit is the count of employers over the limit.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. The $176,100 test is on social security wages, the wage base above which no social security tax is withheld (i1040gi p. 117, line 11; $10,918.20 is 6.2% of $176,100), so `w2.wages` sums Form W-2 box 3 (social security wages) and box 7 (social security tips), the amounts the tax was withheld on. No change to the data.

The $176,100 test is on social security wages, the wage base above which no social security tax is withheld (i1040gi p. 117, line 11; $10,918.20 is 6.2% of $176,100), so w2.wages sums Form W-2 box 3 (social security wages) and box 7 (social security tips) (w2.yaml, 'Add social security wages and social security tips').
